body: Metis, inner moon of Jupiter / S/1979 J 1; distinct from Amalthea, Thebe, Adrastea, asteroid 9 Metis and Solar Orbiter Metis instrument
status: research-only native assessment; no dossier91, embedding, catalogue, globe, shape or codec adoption

products.identity: Five panels: top two Thebe, middle two Amalthea, bottom Metis. Page Target metadata Amalthea is montage scope, not an exclusive Metis identification. Whole publisher product retained, no other moon assigned to Metis map.

publisherStatements.orientation: north approximately up; correct relative sizes

products.inspection: Whole 490x1190 L JPEG inspected: tiny blurred Metis at bottom, separate larger disks above. Brightness/sampling/noise/black gaps are not local grains, chemistry, calibrated visible colour, complete geography or atmosphere absence.
products.limits: Caption says best during 11th orbit in November1997, not current best/latest. Exact raw UTC/filter/exposure/PSF/photometric and shape/frame crosswalk open. Thebe crater/Amalthea bright spots and Io-exposure explanation do not describe Metis. TIFF decoded but not separately visually inspected; no TIFF/JPEG pixel identity claim.

products.identity: Whole retained source already used for Thebe: left Thebe, centre Amalthea, right Metis. Right disk alone identifies Metis; no centre/left terrain transfer.

publisherStatements.orientation: anti-Jupiter sides; north approximately up; sunlight from right

products.inspection: Existing unchanged748x381 L JPEG reinspected with Metis focus. Small irregular right disk is sampled/blurred; not local regolith, colour, local composition or complete coverage. Amalthea overexposed bright patch and Thebe Zethus not Metis.
products.limits: Publisher highest-resolution wording is historical context not independently established current ranking. Raw UTC/filter/PSF/product identity, shape/normal, global registration and photometry open. TIFF/source provenance preserved; no new resampling.

products.identity: Annotated Jupiter main dust ring and Perseus field, not resolved Metis disk or surface. Thin dust bands associated with Metis/Adrastea orbits are context only.
products.inspection: Whole547x548 RGB JPEG inspected: near-monochrome noisy star field, bright diagonal ring and blue Perseus/Algol labels/lines. Annotation is not spectral colour or moon geography; specks not mapped local rocks.
products.limits: No Metis body texture, current shedding rate, independently reproduced photometry, grain chemistry or registered cloud/surface inference. Exact UTC/rawproduct/filter/exposure and particle-versus-star crosswalk open. TIFF decoded not separately visually inspected; no pixel identity asserted.
